title_original: Egypt’s El Gouna Kicks Off MENA Fall Film Festival Season With Local Breakouts, Oscar Contenders & Emerging Talents
editorial_title_zh: 埃及埃尔古纳电影节携本土新片、奥斯卡竞争者与新锐人才开幕，拉开中东和北非秋季电影节季序幕
editorial_excerpt_zh: 中东和北非地区2026年秋季电影节季于今日拉开帷幕，迎来第9届埃尔古纳电影节。本届电影节在同名的埃及红海度假胜地埃尔古纳举行，开幕红毯盛会放映了法国导演马克·菲托西（Marc Fitoussi）执导的剧情片……

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Middle East and North Africa’s 2026 fall film festival season gets underway today with the 9th El Gouna Film Festival.", "links": [{"text": "El Gouna", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/el-gouna/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Unfolding in its namesake Egyptian Red Sea resort of El Gouna, the festival opens with a red-carpet gala screening of French director Marc Fitoussi’s drama All About Corinne , starring Isabelle Huppert as a jobbing actress who strikes up an unexpected friendship with a big screen star."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This edition is Andrew Mohsen’s first in the role of artistic director , replacing respected distributor and exhibitor Marianne Khoury who stepped down from the position earlier this year.", "links": [{"text": "Andrew Mohsen’s first in the role of artistic director", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/04/egypt-el-gouna-film-festival-new-artistic-director-1236771615/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/All-About-Corinne.jpg?w=300", "alt": "'All About Corinne'", "caption": "", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "'All About Corinne' Review: Isabelle Huppert Shines As Movie Extra With Bigger Ambitions In Delightful Take On French Film Industry - He explains that the team has also had its eye on next year’s edition, the festival’s 10th, as it got to work on the 2026 lineup."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Watch on Deadline"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“We were working on two editions, the 9th and 10th, because next year is going to be a very important anniversary for the festival,” he says. “We really asked ourselves what is the identity of El Gouna? What makes El Gouna special?”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "One feather in its cap is El Gouna’s position as the first big film festival in the MENA region’s fall festival calendar, which continues afterwards with Cairo (November 11-20), Doha (Nov 19-27), Marrakech (Nov 20-28) and Carthage in Tunisia (Dec 12-19). The sixth edition of Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Film Festival was due to take place from December 3 to 12 but has been shelved this year .", "links": [{"text": "take place from December 3 to 12 but has been shelved this year", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/09/saudi-arabia-red-sea-film-festival-cancels-2026-edition-1237109142/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“We are the first major international film festival into the region in the last quarter,” he says. “In the beginning, the first three editions were in September. October gives us more opportunity to get films from San Sebastian, Toronto, and Venice… and get some good insights about the films that are also going to campaign for the Oscars.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "El Gouna will showcase 49 features and 19 shorts across the feature narrative, documentary, and short film competitions as well as Out of Competition and Special screenings sidebars."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The competition will showcase 13 films ranging from local drama Safe Exit by Mohammed Hammad, buzzy regional titles such as Palestinian director Rakan Mayasi’s Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep and A-list festival prizewinners and Oscar contenders Markus Schleinzer’s Rose (Austria) and Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland (Poland)."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "UK director Joanna Hogg is president of the jury which also includes Egyptian actress Nahed El Sebaie ( 19B ), Egyptian composer Khaled Hammad ( The Yacoubian Building ), Iraqi-Kurdish director Shawkat Amin Korki ( The Exam ) and Turkish director Yeşim Ustaoğlu ( What Remains )."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mohsen describes Hammad’s contender Safe Exit , about a Cairo-based security guard grappling with the trauma of his parents’ murder in religious and ethnic violence, as one of the most “important” films to come out of Egypt in recent years.", "links": [{"text": "a Cairo-based security guard grappling", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/01/berlinale-mad-world-sales-mohammed-hammad-safe-exit-egypt-1236682546/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“It’s a very bold film. It’s tackling something that we have never seen in this way before in Egyptian cinema,” he says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Musing more generally on cinema coming out of the MENA region, he suggests it has not been a big year in terms of the numbers of Arab-language films coming to fruition."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I feel production is affected. I don’t know if this is because of the war and what’s happening in the region nowadays, or if it’s cyclical,” he says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the wider program a raft of awards season hopefuls will screen in the Out of Competition lineup including Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord (Romania), Halkwat Mustafa’s No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman (Iraq) and Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden (Japan)."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“It’s the sixth time across nine editions, that we’ve secured the MENA premiere of the Palme d’Or winner,” comments Mohsen."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Securing Arab-language premieres is a more competitive process, he says, with productions often promising their MENA debuts to festivals with links to their funders."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mohsen says he is not a fan of the MENA premiere stipulation, suggesting that given the fractured exhibition infrastructure in the region, films should be given the opportunity to circulate as widely as possible through its festivals. That said, he emphasizes that El Gouna has good relations with the other festivals."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Special Screening line up includes feature documentary Dolphins: My Close Encounters, following Swiss marine biologist Angela Ziltener and her decades-long dolphin research conducted in the Red Sea. It is the first shared title in a new strategic partnership between El Gouna and Switzerland’s Zurich Film Festival.", "links": [{"text": "between El Gouna and Switzerland’s Zurich Film", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/08/zurich-el-gouna-film-festivals-strike-strategic-partnership-1237029542/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Industry reach"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Beyond the film program, Mohsen suggests El Gouna’s mid-October slot also makes it a good meeting point for regional professionals, with festival fatigue yet to kick in."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He points to how El Gouna’s CineGouna industry program has gone from strength to strength to encompass five strands of Funding, Forum, Market, Emerging and and a new focus on Series."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ahmed Shawky, Head of CineGouna Funding, El Gouna’s development and coproduction lab, says the industry program is an increasingly important part of the festival’s overall offering."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“It’s been part of the DNA of the festival from start. article_text:
The Middle East and North Africa’s 2026 fall film festival season gets underway today with the 9th El Gouna Film Festival.

Unfolding in its namesake Egyptian Red Sea resort of El Gouna, the festival opens with a red-carpet gala screening of French director Marc Fitoussi’s drama All About Corinne , starring Isabelle Huppert as a jobbing actress who strikes up an unexpected friendship with a big screen star.

This edition is Andrew Mohsen’s first in the role of artistic director , replacing respected distributor and exhibitor Marianne Khoury who stepped down from the position earlier this year.

Related Stories

'All About Corinne' Review: Isabelle Huppert Shines As Movie Extra With Bigger Ambitions In Delightful Take On French Film Industry - Toronto Film Festival

Isabelle Huppert Comedy 'All About Corinne' Sells To U.S. Ahead Of Toronto North American Premiere

Mohsen, who has been in the programming team since 2023, having previously worked at the Cairo Film Festival, is in his element. He explains that the team has also had its eye on next year’s edition, the festival’s 10th, as it got to work on the 2026 lineup.

Watch on Deadline

“We were working on two editions, the 9th and 10th, because next year is going to be a very important anniversary for the festival,” he says. “We really asked ourselves what is the identity of El Gouna? What makes El Gouna special?”

One feather in its cap is El Gouna’s position as the first big film festival in the MENA region’s fall festival calendar, which continues afterwards with Cairo (November 11-20), Doha (Nov 19-27), Marrakech (Nov 20-28) and Carthage in Tunisia (Dec 12-19). The sixth edition of Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Film Festival was due to take place from December 3 to 12 but has been shelved this year .

“We are the first major international film festival into the region in the last quarter,” he says. “In the beginning, the first three editions were in September. October gives us more opportunity to get films from San Sebastian, Toronto, and Venice… and get some good insights about the films that are also going to campaign for the Oscars.”

El Gouna will showcase 49 features and 19 shorts across the feature narrative, documentary, and short film competitions as well as Out of Competition and Special screenings sidebars.

The competition will showcase 13 films ranging from local drama Safe Exit by Mohammed Hammad, buzzy regional titles such as Palestinian director Rakan Mayasi’s Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep and A-list festival prizewinners and Oscar contenders Markus Schleinzer’s Rose (Austria) and Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland (Poland).

UK director Joanna Hogg is president of the jury which also includes Egyptian actress Nahed El Sebaie ( 19B ), Egyptian composer Khaled Hammad ( The Yacoubian Building ), Iraqi-Kurdish director Shawkat Amin Korki ( The Exam ) and Turkish director Yeşim Ustaoğlu ( What Remains ).

Mohsen describes Hammad’s contender Safe Exit , about a Cairo-based security guard grappling with the trauma of his parents’ murder in religious and ethnic violence, as one of the most “important” films to come out of Egypt in recent years.

“It’s a very bold film. It’s tackling something that we have never seen in this way before in Egyptian cinema,” he says.

Musing more generally on cinema coming out of the MENA region, he suggests it has not been a big year in terms of the numbers of Arab-language films coming to fruition.

“I feel production is affected. I don’t know if this is because of the war and what’s happening in the region nowadays, or if it’s cyclical,” he says.

In the wider program a raft of awards season hopefuls will screen in the Out of Competition lineup including Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord (Romania), Halkwat Mustafa’s No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman (Iraq) and Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden (Japan).

“It’s the sixth time across nine editions, that we’ve secured the MENA premiere of the Palme d’Or winner,” comments Mohsen.

Securing Arab-language premieres is a more competitive process, he says, with productions often promising their MENA debuts to festivals with links to their funders.

Mohsen says he is not a fan of the MENA premiere stipulation, suggesting that given the fractured exhibition infrastructure in the region, films should be given the opportunity to circulate as widely as possible through its festivals. That said, he emphasizes that El Gouna has good relations with the other festivals.

The Special Screening line up includes feature documentary Dolphins: My Close Encounters, following Swiss marine biologist Angela Ziltener and her decades-long dolphin research conducted in the Red Sea. It is the first shared title in a new strategic partnership between El Gouna and Switzerland’s Zurich Film Festival.

Industry reach

Beyond the film program, Mohsen suggests El Gouna’s mid-October slot also makes it a good meeting point for regional professionals, with festival fatigue yet to kick in.

He points to how El Gouna’s CineGouna industry program has gone from strength to strength to encompass five strands of Funding, Forum, Market, Emerging and and a new focus on Series.

Ahmed Shawky, Head of CineGouna Funding, El Gouna’s development and coproduction lab, says the industry program is an increasingly important part of the festival’s overall offering.

“It’s been part of the DNA of the festival from start. Now we have a very decent number of attendees for the film program, but when it started it was difficult to think of El Gouna purely as an audience-based festival,” he says, pointing to the festival’s beach resort setting far from major urban centers.

“Bringing in the industry was a brilliant idea that the founders had. It’s also good place for an industry event. The atmosphere is chill. People love to come. It’s less hectic than Cannes or Berlin and then, of course, Egypt is the regional cinema hub.”

“Across the years, Cinegouna has grown from only panels and a co-production platform, to add a market as well as the emerging talents program, and this year, for the first time CineGouna series.”

The Cinegouna Funding strand is hosting 19 projects this year, 13 films in development and six in postproduction, selected from 300 submissions.

Projects in development include Egyptian director Mohamed Siam’s Waiting for Paradise , Lebanese filmmaker Noel Keserwany’s Printemps and Abdallah Al-Khatib’s The Pessoptimists , while films in postproduction include Sofia Djama’s Quarter to Thursday which was supported by CineGouna in development.

Additionally, the strand has also launched two new initiatives, Egyptian Voices for local talents as well as Safe Harbour MENA, in partnership with the International Feature Film Rotterdam.

The latter strand, supporting displaced directors, has invited Hadi Bakhit (Sudan) with The Search for Memory of a Lost Homeland ; Ezel Manay (Syria/Turkey) with Temporary Protection ; Ahmed Nagm Eldin (Sudan/Rwanda/Mauritania) with Sabary; and Yasir Faiz (Sudan/Kenya) with The Martyr’s Wedding .

Highlights of the Forum program include a masterclass with this year’s guest of honor, acting star Mona Zaki; A talk on AI led by Angus Finney; a masterclass by The Lincoln Lawyer , Black Sails and The Old Man director and cinematographer Lukas Ettlin as well as two deep dives into the male and female characters of late director Mohammed Khan and a panel on American Doctor with the participation of director Poh Si Teng.

article_text:
On this week’s episode of The Screen Podcast, we hear from the head of the UK Global Screen Fund (UKGSF) and round up the latest from the BFI London Film Festival (LFF).

Watch above or listen below

To download or subscribe to future episodes, search for ‘The Screen Podcast’, which is available on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , Acast and YouTube .

First, host Wendy Mitchell is joined by Screen reporters Ellie Calnan, Mona Tabbara and Ben Dalton to discuss the industry highlights from the LFF.

Then Tabbara is joined by UKGSF director Denitsa Yordanova to delve into the £18m-a-year initiative which provides funding for international distribution, co-production and business development. She explains what producers and sales agents need to know about the revamped fund.

The Screen Podcast is produced by Ellie Calnan, with Wendy Mitchell serving as editorial director. New episodes every Thursday.

editorial_title_zh: 韩国艺术奖 2026
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "#1. 引言", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "欢迎来到“韩国艺术奖 2026”展览。韩国国立现代美术馆与SBS文化基金会共同主办的韩国艺术奖，是韩国最具声望的艺术奖项与艺术家支持项目之一。自2012年以来，该奖项每年通过四位入选艺术家的创作，为探讨当代艺术核心议题提供了一个备受瞩目的平台。今年的四位艺术家是李海民孙（Lee Hai Min Sun）、李正宇（Lee Jungwoo）、全贤善（Jeon Hyunsun）和洪振宣（Hong Jin-hwon）。尽管他们使用不同的方法和媒介，但这四位艺术家共享着一个极其重要的视角：他们不接受将世界视为一个固定或完成的系统。在他们的作品中，你会发现那些拒绝消失的事物、无法被完全解释的事物，以及仍在成型过程中的事物。他们凝视着隐藏在可见之物底层的裂缝与震颤，并带回那些被擦除或遗漏的存在。当你浏览他们的作品时，你或许会发现自己正面对我们这个时代的真实面貌。从这个意义上说，“韩国艺术奖”不仅是颁发给艺术家的奖项，它更是一个概括了艺术所创造的无尽形态以及艺术所揭示的秘密真理的词句。现在，让我们一起走进展览，步入那令人惊叹的", "translated": true}]

article_text:
#1. Introduction

Welcome to «Korea Artist Prize 2026» exhibition. Co-organized by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea and the SBS Foundation, the Korea Artist Prize is one of the most prestigious art awards and artist support programs in Korea. Since 2012, it has annually provided a prominent platform for exploring the most important issues being addressed by contemporary art through the creative works of four selected artists. This year’s artists are Lee Hai Min Sun, Lee Jungwoo, Jeon Hyunsun, and Hong Jin-hwon. Although they use different methods and media, these four artists share one very important perspective: they do not accept the world as a fixed or completed system. In their work, you will find things that refuse to disappear, things that cannot be fully explained, and things that are still in the process of taking shape. They peer into the cracks and tremors hidden beneath the visible, and bring back entities that have been erased or omitted. As you survey their work, you just might find yourself confronting the true face of our time. In this sense, the «Korea Artist Prize» is more than just an award given to artists; it is a phrase that encapsulates the endless forms that art creates and the secret truths that art reveals. title_original: 【プレビュー】「室町ごころの風景 ―光り輝く四季と連歌懐紙の美―」五島美術館で10月27日から やまと絵屏風と連歌懐紙でひもとく中世の風景美
editorial_title_zh: 【预览】“室町心境之风景——光辉四季与连歌怀纸之美”10月27日起在五岛美术馆举办 以大和绘屏风与连歌怀纸解读中世纪风景之美
editorial_excerpt_zh: 五岛美术馆（东京都世田谷区）将于10月27日起举办特别展“室町心境之风景——光辉四季与连歌怀纸之美”。室町时代大和绘屏风所描绘的四季与景物母题，也见于中世纪的料纸装饰，以及记录室町时代大流行的连歌的连歌怀纸之中。

article_text:
五島美術館（東京都世田谷区）で、特別展「室町ごころの風景 ―光り輝く四季と連歌懐紙の美―」が10月27日から開催されます。

室町時代のやまと絵屏風に描かれた四季や景物のモティーフは、中世の料紙装飾、そして室町時代に大流行した連歌を記した連歌懐紙にも見られます。なかでも下絵が施された連歌懐紙には四季や景物が、ときに句と響き合うように金銀泥で描かれており、室町時代における文藝と美術の交差の一端がうかがえます。

連歌は、和歌の上の句（五・七・五）と下の句（七・七）を、個人の詠作ではなく別々のひとが詠み、つないでいく形式の文藝で、室町時代に最盛期を迎えました。複数人で集まり、即興で句を詠み継ぎながら全体として一つの作品をつくりあげる連歌の共同創作は、参加者の心を結び、人々は連想のように次々と展開されることばとイメージの変奏を楽しみました。

本展は、四季モティーフの宝庫とも言われる連歌懐紙の下絵に注目し、その魅力を探るこれまでにない展覧会です。同時代のやまと絵屏風、連歌にまつわる諸作品を通じて、「室町ごころ」の風景を展望します。連歌を通して見えてくる室町文化と美術の一側面が紹介されます。

特別展「室町ごころの風景 ―光り輝く四季と連歌懐紙の美―」

会場：五島美術館（東京都世田谷区上野毛3-9-25）

会期：2026年10月27日（火）～12月6日（日） ※会期中一部展示替があります

開館時間：10:00～17:00（入館は16:30まで）

休館日：月曜日（11/23は開館）、11/24

入館料：一般1400円／高・大学生1100円／中学生以下無料 ※障害者手帳をお持ちの方、ならびに介助者の方1名は200円引

アクセス：東急大井町線（各駅停車）「上野毛駅」下車徒歩約5分

詳細は、 五島美術館公式サイト まで。

本展でのおすすめ作品

重要文化財 浜松図 屏風

浜松図は、やまと絵の画題の一つで海浜の景に松林を描いた絵です。本品は、色とりどりの四季の草花、60羽を超える小鳥、人々の生活の営みも描きこまれているところに特色があります。画面には雲母を掃き、小さな金の箔片を用いた装飾的効果によって、朗らかな明るさのある光景が広がります。特定の場所の実景というわけではなく、室町時代の人々の理想の景色を描いているのかもしれません。

重要文化財 瀟湘八景 遠浦帰帆図 玉澗 筆・同賛

連歌の叙景句や心得について、水墨画や瀟湘八景を例に挙げて説明されることもありました。本品は、「東山御物」を代表する唐絵の名品の一つとして知られますが、足利将軍家から流出後、一時期、連歌師である 宗長 （1448～1532）が所持していたという伝来があります。連歌師と絵画の接点を示唆する作品です。

重要文化財 染田天神講 連歌関係資料

大和国山辺郡東山内の有力武士、 多田 順実 （？～1408）は天神信仰に篤く、旅人より天神御影がもたらされたことをきっかけに天神講を結成しました。それから当地では約200年間、天神講による連歌奉納が行われていました。本品はその遺品です。人々が連歌を詠む背景にある天神信仰、用いた道具、講を維持するための約束事、地方連歌としての作例等、連歌を多角的に考えるうえで貴重な資料群です。

新撰菟玖波集 三条西実隆 筆

宗祇 ら撰の准勅撰連歌集。明応4年（1495）成立。『新撰菟玖波集』の編纂事情は、三条西実隆の日記『 実隆公記 』によって知られています。実隆のほか、 兼載 、 肖柏 、 宗長 など、宗祇の弟子の連歌師らが編纂に関わりました。『実隆公記』明応8年（1499）6月8日の条に、宗祇の依頼で『新撰菟玖波集』を写した記事があり、本書と推定されています。成立から間もない時期の伝本として大変貴重です。

五・七・五と七・七の句を即興でつなぎ、人々の心と想像力を結びつけながら紡ぎ出された中世の連歌。本展は、これまで単独で深くスポットが当てられる機会の少なかった連歌懐紙の下絵に焦点を当て、同時代のやまと絵屏風や名宝とともに「室町ごころ」の豊かな精神風景を体感できる貴重な機会です。秋深まる五島美術館の庭園とともに、金銀に輝く料紙の上で繰り広げられる繊細な季節のうつろいや、連歌師たちが愛した風景美の広がりを堪能してみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
Seth Rogen has made projects about the end of the world and anthropomorphized grocery store items , but the new hand-drawn, black-and-white animated film “ Tangles ,” a drama about a woman returning to her small conservative town to take care of her mother who has Alzheimer’s disease, might be closest to in his heart. In conversation at the Middleburg Film Festival this weekend, the producer shared how the specific approach that director Leah Nelson and her co-screenwriters Sarah Leavitt and Trev Renney was more of a selling point than a deterrent.

“To me, animation is a medium and it is my instinct to trust the creative ambitions and instincts of the people that I work with and to not question them too much, honestly. And if anything, I have tried to train myself to really go on the journey with people’s creative instincts, even if they are not my own or even if they seem like you could argue against them,” said Rogen. “This film being an animated film is the perfect example of that. You probably could have talked them out of this. You probably could have argued there are surreal sequences [that] you could probably do in live-action if you really wanted to. There’s visual effects, you can make a wave come into a room. It’s not impossible.”

The opportunity for Rogen and his wife, director Lauren Miller Rogen , to produce the film came about from the advocacy work they’ve done for Alzheimer research. The couple met Nelson and Leavitt, who wrote the graphic novel that the film is based on, “Tangles: A Story About Alzheimer’s, My Mother and Me,” at a charity event, and stayed in touch with them to develop the film adaptation, and fundraise for it over time.

Talking more about the film taking what some may see as an unconventional approach to the material, even from an animation perspective, Rogen said, “Truthfully, they came to us wanting it to be animated. It was based on a graphic novel. They had a look, they had a vision. And rather than try to poke holes in that, we all chose to support it. And rather than say, ‘Why does this have to be animated?’ We all thought, ‘Wow, very interesting. What an interesting approach to this.’ It’s more unique, it’s more specific.”

He continued, “The more I make things, the word ‘specificity’ is the thing that I am telling the people I work with the most to seek and to try to create in their own work. What makes it specific to you and to this? What makes it different [from] what anyone else would do to tell this story? What makes it distinct? And so all those things, animation, that’s specific, black and white, that’s specific. Hand drawn, that’s specific. And I think in art, the more specific art is, the more it seems to resonate.”

Rogen used examples of other famous artists working in different mediums to support his theory. “Andy Warhol isn’t the best painter. He’s one of the most specific painters. Jackson Pollock you can argue is not even a good painter, but it’s unbelievably specific. You see it, you know who did it right away. And that’s to me the key of specificity. And I think with this, you see one frame of it, you know what it is,” he said.

Speaking again about “Tangles,” the producer said, “You could put 10 movies on the screen. If this was one of them, the specificity of it is what would make you instantly recognize it. And to me, that has become, as I’ve worked more and more, something that I’ve really looked to and encouraged those who I work with to pursue, is not just creative ambition or clarity or any of that. All those things as well, but also what can you do to make this specific? What can you do? What are all the things you could do, all the parameters you can put on it that will set it apart from anyone else’s version of this were they to do it?”

“Tangles,” which includes the voices of Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Abbi Jacobson, Bryan Cranston, Beanie Feldstein, and Rogen himself, premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in May , and was eventually acquired by IFC in August, just in time to mount a Best Animated Feature Oscar campaign.

article_text:
The Image Centre in Toronto invites Canadian and international scholars, researchers and artists to apply for six fellowships supporting original research across its extensive photography collections, with opportunities ranging from artistic research to postdoctoral study.

Open Call:

Applications are open for The Image Centre’s 2027 Research Fellowships, offering researchers and artists the opportunity to work directly with significant photographic collections and archives in Toronto, Canada.

Six competitive fellowships are available for 2027, accommodating applicants at different stages of academic and artistic practice. Research may draw on The Image Centre’s holdings and, where relevant, the collections of Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections.

The opportunities include the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship, Penny Rubinoff Fellowship, Elaine Ling Fellowship, Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research, and Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship.

Institutional Context:

Since 2014, the Image Centre at Toronto Metropolitan University has offered fellowships supporting photography-related research.

Its holdings include the acclaimed Black Star Collection, comprising more than a quarter-million photojournalistic prints spanning the twentieth century, alongside historic and fine art photography collections and archives devoted to photographers including Werner Wolff, Jo Spence, Wendy Snyder MacNeil, Berenice Abbott, Minna Keene, Violet Keene Perinchief and Richard Harrington.

The 2027 programme also introduces the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, developed with the Archive of Modern Conflict, which enables research across internationally significant photographic collections in Toronto and London.

Eligibility and Criteria:

All six fellowships are open to Canadian and international applicants, although individual eligibility requirements vary.

The IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship requires a PhD and provides a full-time, one-year research opportunity.

The Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship is open to applicants holding a PhD.

The Penny Rubinoff Fellowship requires a master’s degree. Current PhD students and candidates may apply, but applicants who already hold a PhD and postdoctoral researchers are not eligible.

The Elaine Ling Fellowship is intended for current master’s students and recent master’s graduates. Doctoral students, PhD holders and postdoctoral researchers are ineligible.

The Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research is open to applicants at any level of education, including independent artists with relevant experience and demonstrated interests. Artists seeking to conduct artistic research within the collections are specifically encouraged to apply for this fellowship.

The Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship is open to applicants who hold or are working towards at least an undergraduate degree and/or are photo-based artists. Research should contribute new perspectives on women photographers, including Wendy Snyder MacNeil.

Evaluation Process:

Applications are evaluated according to the clarity and strength of the proposed research plan, originality and creativity, engagement with primary sources in The Image Centre’s collections, the applicant’s ability to undertake the research, and the specificity of the proposed research outcomes.

The selection committee includes representatives from The Image Centre and Toronto Metropolitan University, alongside an external curator or scholar.

Applicants must apply for the fellowship appropriate to their research and eligibility. Blanket applications for multiple fellowships will not be considered. Previous recipients of an Image Centre Fellowship may not reapply for five years following submission of their previous final report.

Practical Information:

Funding and residency periods vary by fellowship.

IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship: $70,000 CAD annual salary plus benefits. The full-time fellowship runs from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2028 and includes additional research funding for work in London.

Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship: $10,000 CAD. Research period of one to three months.

Penny Rubinoff Fellowship: $5,000 CAD. Research period of two to six weeks.

Elaine Ling Fellowship: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.

Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.

Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.

Except for the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, research residencies take place between 15 February and 15 December 2027 . Fellows are responsible for travel and accommodation expenses, and the fellowship stipends are intended to help offset these costs. International fellows are responsible for obtaining any required visas.

Applications and Queries:

For the Nadir Mohamed, Penny Rubinoff, Elaine Ling, Howard Tanenbaum and Wendy Snyder MacNeil Fellowships, applicants must submit a research proposal of approximately 1,000 words, a CV, a writing sample of up to 20 pages and one letter of recommendation. Artists applying for the Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship may submit a portfolio of up to ten images or film or video work of up to ten minutes instead of a writing sample.

Applications and reference letters must be received by 18 October 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST .

Deadline: 18 October 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST Location: Toronto, Canada Programme: The Image Centre Research Fellowships 2027 Number of fellowships: Six Eligibility: Canadian and international applicants Funding: From $4,000 CAD to $70,000 CAD plus benefits, depending on fellowship Applications and general enquiries: imagecentre.research@torontomu.ca Collection enquiries: imagecentre.collects@torontomu.ca

For more information, please refer to the official website .

映画チケットを U-NEXTでお得にゲット PR

解説・あらすじ

「ハイキック・ガール！」「KG カラテガール」など数々のアクション映画で活躍してきた武田梨奈が、暗殺者役で主演を務めたクライムアクション。 天涯孤独のレイは、小さな海辺の町で時計の修理屋として働きながら、ひっそりと暮らしている。しかし彼女の正体は凄腕の暗殺者で、バーの店主から殺しの依頼を受けては確実に標的を仕留めてきた。一方、幼少期をレイと施設で共に過ごした男も同じ町に住んでおり、彼女のライバルとして暗殺業をこなしていた。レイは町にやってきたある男と宿命の出会いを果たし、彼に惹かれていく。 主人公レイ役の武田がCG・ワイヤーなしでバトルアクションとガンアクションを熱演し、レイと宿命の出会いを果たす男をダンス＆ボーカルグループ「FANTASTICS」の瀬口黎弥、レイと同じ裏社会に生きる孤独な暗殺者を萩原聖人が演じる。共演に嶋田久作、有森也実、特別出演に布施博。監督・脚本は「ニート・ニート・ニート」「殺る女」の宮野ケイジ。

title_original: 東京都現代美術館でソ・ドホ展やブライアン・イーノ展が開催へ。2027年度の展覧会ラインアップが公開
editorial_title_zh: 徐道获与布莱恩·伊诺等展将在东京都现代美术馆举办，2027年度展览阵容公布
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/ddc74757/cbc4e683-b251-49ec-9097-b414397c5ea5.jpg?w=2352&q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "东京都现代美术馆公布了2027年度举办的展览日程的第一弹。", "links": [{"text": "東京都現代美術館", "url": "https://www.tokyoartbeat.com/venues/-/4A4AABB8"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为该馆2026年度的展览，此前已公布将举办：作为1960年代纽约观念艺术核心人物的汉斯·哈克（1936〜）的亚洲首个大规模个人回顾展（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）；与致力于推动包括性少数群体在内的所有人实现共存和平等的Sunpride基金会共同主办的展览（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）；以及聚焦于呼应个人及社会记忆的行为艺术的“MOT Annual 2027”（2027年2月20日〜5月30日）。在此，本文将介绍本次新公布的2027年度举办的3个展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "徐道获展（暂定名）／2027年6月19日〜9月26日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以伦敦为据点活跃于国际舞台的韩裔艺术家徐道获（1962〜）在日本国内规模最大、也是首都圈美术馆的首场个人回顾展。目前其在韩国国立现代美术馆首尔馆举办的展览也引发了热议。本展将展出运用半透明布料按原尺寸复原建筑空间的装置艺术，以及绘画和影像作品等多元作品，探寻这位长期探讨“家”与“身份认同”不断变化状态的艺术家的世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/ddc74757/cbc4e683-b251-49ec-9097-b414397c5ea5.jpg?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "布莱恩·伊诺展（暂定名）／2027年11月3日〜2028年3月5日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "布莱恩·伊诺（1948〜）在拓展音乐与视觉艺术边界的同时，对现代各个创意领域产生了深远影响。本展在伊诺本人的全面协助下，对其职业生涯的全貌进行审视，这也是全球首个在美术馆举办的正规回顾展。展览将“环境音乐”（Ambient）所体现的理念视为贯穿音乐、光影、影像、空间及生成系统的创作原理，尝试探讨为了理解复杂且不可预测的世界、并在其不间断的流动中生存下去，艺术当下究竟能做些什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "MOT Plus项目（暂定名）／①②2027年6月19日〜9月26日，③2027年10月26日〜11月23日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“MOT Plus”是一项自2025年度起实施的持续性项目，旨在为当代艺术的广泛风格与表现形式提供全新的欣赏方式。2027年度，该项目将利用策划展厅，免费向公众开放3个不同的展示项目：①国内研究成果展、②与汉·内夫肯斯基金会合作呈献的亚洲影像艺术家新作展、③馆藏装置艺术作品特别展。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/ddc74757/cbc4e683-b251-49ec-9097-b414397c5ea5.jpg?w=2352&q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東京都現代美術館 で2027年度に開催される展覧会スケジュールの第1弾が公開された。", "links": [{"text": "東京都現代美術館", "url": "https://www.tokyoartbeat.com/venues/-/4A4AABB8"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同館では2026年度の展覧会として、1960年代ニューヨークのコンセプチュアル・アートの中心人物であったハンス・ハーケ（1936〜）のアジア初の大規模個展（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）、性的マイノリティを含むすべての人々の共存と平等の実現に貢献することをミッションに掲げるサンプライド財団との共催展（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）、個人や社会の記憶を呼応させるパフォーマンスに焦点を当てる「MOTアニュアル2027」（2027年2月20日〜5月30日）の開催がこれまでに発表されていた。ここでは、このたび明らかになった、2027年度開催の3つの展覧会を紹介する。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "ソ・ドホ展（仮称）／2027年6月19日〜9月26日"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ロンドンを拠点に国際的に活躍する韓国出身のアーティスト、ソ・ドホ（1962〜）の国内では過去最大規模、首都圏の美術館では初となる個展。現在、韓国の国立現代美術館ソウル館で開催中の展覧会も話題を呼んでいる同作家。本展では、半透明の布を用いて建築空間を原寸大に再現したインスタレーションをはじめ、ドローイングや映像作品など多様な作品を展示し、「ホーム」や「アイデンティティ」の変化し続ける在り方を探求してきた作家の世界を探る。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/ddc74757/cbc4e683-b251-49ec-9097-b414397c5ea5.jpg?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "ブライアン・イーノ展（仮称）／2027年11月3日〜2028年3月5日"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "音楽と視覚芸術の境界を拡張しながら、現代の様々な創造的領域に影響を与えてきたブライアン・イーノ（1948〜）。本展は、イーノ本人の全面的な協力のもと、そのキャリアの全貌を検証するもので、美術館での本格的な回顧展としては世界初となる。展覧会では、「アンビエント」に体現される思想を音楽、光、映像、空間、生成的システムを貫く創造原理としてとらえ、複雑で予測不能な世界を理解し、その絶え間ない流動のなかで生きるために、芸術にいま何ができるのかを探ることを試みるという。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "MOT Plusプロジェクト（仮称）／①②2027年6月19日〜9月26日、③2027年10月26日〜11月23日"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「MOT Plus」は、現代美術の幅広い様式や表現の新たな鑑賞方法を提示する継続的な取り組みとして、2025年度から実施されている事業。2027年度は企画展示室を使い、①国内リサーチ成果展、②ハン・ネフケンス財団との共同によるアジアの映像作家の新作展、③収蔵インスタレーション作品の特別展示という3つの異なる展示プロジェクトを無料公開する。"}]
article_text:
東京都現代美術館 で2027年度に開催される展覧会スケジュールの第1弾が公開された。

同館では2026年度の展覧会として、1960年代ニューヨークのコンセプチュアル・アートの中心人物であったハンス・ハーケ（1936〜）のアジア初の大規模個展（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）、性的マイノリティを含むすべての人々の共存と平等の実現に貢献することをミッションに掲げるサンプライド財団との共催展（2027年2月6日〜5月16日）、個人や社会の記憶を呼応させるパフォーマンスに焦点を当てる「MOTアニュアル2027」（2027年2月20日〜5月30日）の開催がこれまでに発表されていた。ここでは、このたび明らかになった、2027年度開催の3つの展覧会を紹介する。

ソ・ドホ展（仮称）／2027年6月19日〜9月26日

ロンドンを拠点に国際的に活躍する韓国出身のアーティスト、ソ・ドホ（1962〜）の国内では過去最大規模、首都圏の美術館では初となる個展。現在、韓国の国立現代美術館ソウル館で開催中の展覧会も話題を呼んでいる同作家。本展では、半透明の布を用いて建築空間を原寸大に再現したインスタレーションをはじめ、ドローイングや映像作品など多様な作品を展示し、「ホーム」や「アイデンティティ」の変化し続ける在り方を探求してきた作家の世界を探る。

ブライアン・イーノ展（仮称）／2027年11月3日〜2028年3月5日

音楽と視覚芸術の境界を拡張しながら、現代の様々な創造的領域に影響を与えてきたブライアン・イーノ（1948〜）。本展は、イーノ本人の全面的な協力のもと、そのキャリアの全貌を検証するもので、美術館での本格的な回顧展としては世界初となる。展覧会では、「アンビエント」に体現される思想を音楽、光、映像、空間、生成的システムを貫く創造原理としてとらえ、複雑で予測不能な世界を理解し、その絶え間ない流動のなかで生きるために、芸術にいま何ができるのかを探ることを試みるという。

MOT Plusプロジェクト（仮称）／①②2027年6月19日〜9月26日、③2027年10月26日〜11月23日

「MOT Plus」は、現代美術の幅広い様式や表現の新たな鑑賞方法を提示する継続的な取り組みとして、2025年度から実施されている事業。2027年度は企画展示室を使い、①国内リサーチ成果展、②ハン・ネフケンス財団との共同によるアジアの映像作家の新作展、③収蔵インスタレーション作品の特別展示という3つの異なる展示プロジェクトを無料公開する。

article_text:
Franz von Saalfeld erschafft heitere Szenerien mit düsteren Untertönen und war 2022 Documenta-Teilnehmer. Nun sind seine Arbeiten in der Goldstein Galerie in Frankfurt am Main zu sehen

Über 80 Jahre ist es her, dass Jean Dubuffet von der "rohen Kunst" sprach und damit Kunst in den Fokus rückte, die jenseits des klassischen Betriebs entsteht. Mit "Art Brut" oder "Outsider Art" ist meist eine Kunst gemeint, die jenseits des klassischen Betriebs entsteht. Oft autodidaktisch. Aber wer sind hier eigentlich die Außenseiter, oder wer steht da außerhalb von was? Sollten wir über die Biografien oder besser über die Kunst reden? In dieser Serie stellen wir Künstlerinnen und Künstler aus Frankfurt am Main vor, die einen ganz eigenen Zugang zur Öffentlichkeit gefunden haben.

Es gibt diesen Moment, in dem man scheinbar aus einem Traum erwacht, nur um irgendwann festzustellen, dass man immer noch träumt. False awakening , falsches Erwachen, heißt dieses Phänomen. In einem solchen kann man sich manches Szenario vorstellen, das Franz von Saalfeld aufs Papier bringt. Da wird in großer Selbstverständlichkeit ein Delfin aufgeschlitzt (zu sehen 2022 auf der Documenta Fifteen, die Stadt Kassel hat die Arbeit zusammen mit elf weiteren aus dem Atelier Goldstein angekauft). Auf einem anderen Blatt wird im Vorbeigehen einem verkleideten Wesen ein Schlag in die Magengrube verpasst.

Es gibt aber auch unzählige schlicht sehr lustige Szenerien, teils Grotesken, oder solche, bei denen die Heiterkeit nicht von der Verunsicherung zu trennen ist. Igel machen sich an Menschen zu schaffen, sie klettern senkrecht an Wartenden hoch, die vor einer Konditorei die wunderbare Auslage bewundern.

Ein bevorzugtes Sujet scheinen Menschenmengen jeder Couleur zu sein: Warteschlangen vorm Zahnarzt, vor der Bäckerei, Aufmärsche mit Blasmusik oder Karneval. Und das Sonnenbaden spielt bei Franz von Saalfeld auch immer wieder eine Rolle.

Unbestimmte Orte und Zeiten

Der Künstler arbeitet vorwiegend mit Aquarellfarbe und Zeichenstift, daneben entstehen Dioramen aus Häusern und ein umfangreiches Skript in Textform. Die Kleinstadtidylle ist in diesen Werken, die von kompakten Beobachtungen bis zu großformatigen Panoramen reichen, oft nicht weit, aber nie ganz zu fassen.

Einmal habe ich Franz von Saalfeld in seinem Atelier besucht, das er seit vielen Jahren in der Frankfurter Ateliergemeinschaft Goldstein bezogen hat - einem Angebot der Lebenshilfe Frankfurt, bei dem explizit künstlerisch gearbeitet wird . Zu viel wollte ich den Künstler nicht fragen – er arbeitet hoch konzentriert, man will ihn nicht dabei stören. Und dann die freilich unbegründete Angst, das Enigma, die Rätselhaftigkeit dieser Bilder aufzulösen. Das sei "Irgendwo", antwortete von Saalfeld auf meine Frage, ob sich all dies an einem bestimmten Ort abspiele.

In diesem Konglomerat aus nicht näher bestimmten Kleinstädten also gibt es noch Fachgeschäfte für alles Mögliche und ein reges Vereinsleben. Die Mutter ruft ihre Familie schon mal mit altertümlichen Sprüchen zu Tisch oder an die reich gedeckte Kaffeetafel. Offenbar ist man nicht nur Ort, sondern auch Zeit entrückt. Eine ebenso unbestimmte Vergangenheit scheint hier Einzug zu halten. Vielleicht eine, die auch für ihren Schöpfer nie real war, sondern durch andere Bilder und Erzählungen vermittelt.

Text als potenzierte Seltsamkeit

Franz von Saalfeld stammt aus einer Künstlerfamilie, die das Zeichnen und Schreiben früh förderte. 1961 wurde er in Ingelheim geboren, wo er bis heute lebt und wochentags nach Frankfurt ins Atelier pendelt. Sein Vater arbeitete als Karikaturist – vielleicht ist es auch dieser hintergründige Humor, den man im Werk seines Sohnes wiederfindet.

Zu Eröffnungen wird bei von Saalfeld gerne musiziert, früher mit der ganzen Familie. "Wer die Welt kennt" heißt seine aktuelle Ausstellung in der Goldstein Galerie. Sie zeigt Arbeiten, in denen Worte eine Rolle spielen. Nur ein kleiner Teil des Werks umfasst Text, darunter kleine Comicstrips, die manchmal unvermittelt aufhören, kommentierte Szenerien oder Landkarten. Meist fügt der Text Franz von Saalfelds Bildern eine Ebene hinzu. Oft potenziert er deren Seltsamkeit nur noch.

Vom alten, unheimlichen Amerika schrieb Popkritiker Greil Marcus. Wenn es eine alte, unheimliche Bundesrepublik Deutschland gibt, dann muss sie in den Werken von Franz von Saalfeld beheimatet sein. Versatzstücke einer realen BRD werden hier nach eigener Künstlerlogik neu zusammengesetzt.

Gewalt, Siamkatzen und Fasching

Manchmal brodelt die Gewalt unter der Oberfläche, aber dann geht es auch sehr lang und ausführlich um Siamkatzen und Fasching. Gut möglich also, dass es bloß die eigene permanente Verunsicherung dieser Tage ist, die man in der Kunst zu entdecken meint.

Und dann immer wieder der Humor. In einem Diptychon stellt Franz von Saalfeld den so im Bild betitelten "Künstlermarkt" dem Neologismus des "Marktkünstlers" gegenüber. Bestehendes und Bekanntes greift von Saalfeld auf und dichtet es in unendlicher Variation um – in dieser Welt liegt Amorbach direkt neben Amokslauf und das uns noch unbekannte Drecksfelde, klar, an der Drecke.

热门文章", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和表示，他在处理儿童演员的方法上变得更加灵活。在拍摄《小偷家族》以及他在海外执导的电影《真相》和《掮客》时，他没有给孩子们剧本。相反，他根据在试镜中遇到的孩子的个性和词汇量重写了台词，让他们只说出自己能够深信不疑的话，然后才在片场喂词，或者描述一个情境让他们自由交谈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在拍摄《怪物》时，他给了年轻演员剧本，因为他认为这个题材的风险足够大，将孩子与他们的角色隔离开来会更安全。他说，他现在会针对不同的孩子和不同的电影做出具体决定。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有两位导演塑造了这种方法。是枝裕和说，侯孝贤会在一场戏中孩子们玩耍时加入进去，等镜头一开始滚动就悄悄溜走，让他们继续玩下去——是枝裕和现在自己也在使用这个小技巧。", "links": [{"text": "Hou Hsiao-hsien", "url": "https://variety.com/t/hou-hsiao-hsien/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从肯·洛奇那里，他学到了关于判断力的一课。在洛奇的《凯斯》中，一个男孩发现自己抚养的鸟被哥哥杀死后扔进了垃圾桶，这个年轻演员的反应看起来一点也不像是在表演。大约20年前，当是枝裕和在拍摄《无人知晓》并正为此类问题苦恼时，他见到了洛奇，洛奇告诉他，自己当时只指示那个男孩去寻找那只失踪的鸟。当被问及他是如何权衡其中的伦理时，洛奇表示他了解其中的风险，但他确信自己与男孩之间的关系能够修复任何伤害。是枝裕和说，这一课告诉他，洛奇是在边拍边权衡每一个镜头。", "links": [{"text": "Ken Loach", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ken-loach/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我牢牢记住一点：用那种方式去进行判断——上一次拍摄管用所以这一次也管用，或者对上一个孩子管用的方法对这个也管用——是指导儿童演员时最危险的事情，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他说，他从不对孩子们发火，也从不催促他们，更不会对他们撒谎。“理想的状态是，一个孩子在结束一天的工作时会说：‘今天的拍摄真好玩，我很期待明天，’”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他补充说，有些孩子就是不听话，在这种情况下，他会把这一点融入角色中。在为《如父如子》试镜时，有个男孩对所有的提问——包括他的名字和来自哪里——都回答“为什么？”工作人员认为根本无法沟通，但是枝裕和却被他吸引了，并写了一个对什么都回答“为什么”的角色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和自称是侯孝贤的影迷，而非受到他的影响，但这位台湾导演确实改变了他处理一场戏的方式。侯孝贤读了是枝裕和1995年的处女作《幻之光》的剧本（该片在威尼斯电影节上荣获金色奥赛拉奖），并为他介绍了一位作曲家，于是是枝裕和将拍好的成片拿给侯孝贤看。他说，侯孝贤进行了严厉的批评。“我泄气了。但他对我说的话绝对是正确的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和表示，他曾拟定过一份详尽的蓝图，剧组也以专业的工作将其付诸现实，但他却没能在片场更新这个计划。侯孝贤问他是否为每个镜头都画了分镜，并且完全照着画的拍了。他的确是这么做的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“你从哪个角度拍摄一场戏——你走进取景地，去感受那个空间，看光线是如何落在那里的，正是在那个时候，你才第一次决定演员如何移动，”是枝裕和回忆侯孝贤对他说的话。“一旦演员的移动路线决定了，你才能决定机位。你必须按这个顺序来。你知道的，你拍过纪录片。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“现在我真的非常感激他对我说过那些话，但当时它确实狠狠打击了我，”是枝裕和说。“我发誓再也不画分镜头了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和说，他将自己2026年的两部电影《盒中羊》和《再见绘梨》视作回归初心。《盒中羊》入围了戛纳电影节，讲述了一对夫妇的7岁儿子在两年前去世，他们收养了一个根据其数据建造的仿生机器人的故事。是枝裕和表示，尽管有AI元素，但这部电影讲的是悲伤疗愈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这是一个关于如何好好向死者告别的故事，所以我感觉它最终其实最接近我在处女作中尝试做的事情，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“《再见绘本》是他对藤本树（Fujimoto Tatsuki）关于两个因热爱画漫画而结缘的女孩的漫画的真人版改编，曾在威尼斯电影节主竞赛单元展映，并将于在电影节放映后于10月29日在新加坡上映。他表示，在该片中，他带着早期电影的纪录片思维回归，将摄影机视为一只眼睛，纯粹去思考该从何处注视拍摄对象。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“所以我认为我职业生涯的后半程大概从明年开始，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和表示，他最擅长在长途飞行中以及在海外酒店的闲暇时间写作，并且在这次从伦敦前往泰国和新加坡的旅途中也一直在写作。他希望最早能在明年这个时候左右开始拍摄一个项目，如果这很难实现，则在后年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在他开始拍电影30年后，越来越多的职业成就奖让他感到内心不安，他说。“我感觉自己的职业生涯好像还剩大约一半，但同时又感觉好像有人在告诉我，是时候毕业了，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和表示，他对人工智能几乎没有兴趣，尽管《箱中羊》里包含了一个通过生成式人工智能复活的孩子。在一位制片人的建议下，他第一次让AI阅读了他的剧本。“起工时它告诉我，‘这太棒了，这绝对是入围戛纳电影节的稳妥之作，’”他说。他最终结束了这项试验，因为他断定这个AI大概从未有过足以改变其人生的观影经历。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是枝裕和表示，他从不试图揣摩观众想要什么，他引用了他在电视圈时期一位令他敬佩的前辈给他的建议——当时收视率被视为一切。“他告诉我，‘如果你把他们当成观众，那就谁也触动不了，’”是枝裕和说道。“他说要想象一个人的面孔，并为那个人创作。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当被问及他会为死后世界选择什么菜肴（这是对他的1998年电影《下一站，天国》的致意）时，是枝裕和表示，他死后大概什么也不会吃。不过，他临终前的最后一餐已经决定了：位于东京赤坂地区的面馆“砂场”（Sunaba）的天凉面，当年他还是一个连续几天没回家的年轻副导演时，一位资深制片人曾带他去那里。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我在那儿吃过的荞麦面是我一生中吃过最好的，现在依然如此，”他说。“我希望在最后时刻再吃一次那个。”", "translated": true}]

Previous recipients include Im Kwon-taek, Garin Nugroho, Jafar Panahi and Deepa Mehta."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Popular on Variety"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kore-eda said his methods with children have grown more flexible. Through “Shoplifters” and the films he made abroad, “The Truth” and “Broker,” he did not hand children scripts. Instead, he rewrote dialogue around the personality and vocabulary of the children he met at auditions, so that they only spoke lines they could say with conviction, and then fed them lines on set or described a situation and let them talk freely."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "On “Monster,” he gave the young cast scripts, judging that the subject was risky enough that separating the children from their roles was safer. He now decides child by child and film by film, he said."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Two directors shaped that approach. Hou Hsiao-hsien , Kore-eda said, joins in when children are playing in a scene, slips out once the camera is rolling and lets them keep going – a trick Kore-eda now uses himself.", "links": [{"text": "Hou Hsiao-hsien", "url": "https://variety.com/t/hou-hsiao-hsien/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "From Ken Loach , he took a lesson about judgment. In Loach’s “Kes,” a boy discovers the bird he has raised dumped in a trash can after his brother kills it, and the young actor’s reaction looks nothing like a performance. When Kore-eda met Loach about 20 years ago, while he was making “Nobody Knows” and wrestling with similar questions, Loach told him he had only instructed the boy to go and look for the missing bird. Asked how he had weighed the ethics of that, Loach said he understood the risk but was confident that his relationship with the boy could repair any hurt. Kore-eda said the lesson was that Loach was weighing each shot as he went.", "links": [{"text": "Ken Loach", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ken-loach/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I keep it firmly in mind that judging things that way – it worked on the last shoot so it will work this time, or a method that worked with the last child will work with this one – is the most dangerous thing in directing children,” he said."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He never gets angry with children or rushes them, he said, and he doesn’t lie to them. “The ideal is that a child ends the day saying, ‘Today’s shoot was fun, I’m looking forward to tomorrow,’” he said."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Some children simply won’t listen, he added, in which case he turns that into the role. During auditions for “Like Father, Like Son,” one boy answered every question, including his name and where he was from, with “Why?” Staff thought communication was impossible, but Kore-eda was drawn to him and wrote a character who answers everything with “Why?”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kore-eda called himself a fan of Hou rather than someone he was influenced by, but the Taiwanese director also changed how he approaches a scene. Hou read the script for Kore-eda’s 1995 debut “Maborosi,” which won the Golden Osella in Venice, and introduced him to a composer, so Kore-eda showed him the finished film. Hou critiqued it severely, he said. “I was deflated. But what he told me was absolutely right.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kore-eda said he had drawn up a meticulous blueprint and that his crew did professional work to realize it, but he failed to update the plan on set. Hou asked whether he had storyboarded every scene and shot it exactly as drawn. He had."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Where you shoot a scene from – you go into the location, feel the space, see the light falling there, and that’s when you first decide how the actors move,” Kore-eda recalled Hou telling him. “Once the actors’ movements are decided, only then do you decide the camera position. You have to do it in that order. You know that, you made documentaries.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Now I’m truly grateful he said that to me, but at the time it really got to me,” Kore-eda said. “I swore I’d never draw storyboards again.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kore-eda said he sees his two 2026 films, “Sheep in the Box” and “Look Back,” as a return to his roots. “Sheep in the Box,” which competed in Cannes, follows a couple whose 7-year-old son died two years earlier and who take in a humanoid robot built from his data. article_text:
Japanese auteur Kore-eda Hirokazu , whose films are known for their natural performances from child actors, said there is one thing he has decided never to put on screen: a child crying.

“It’s not that I can’t, or that it’s difficult. I don’t shoot it,” the Japanese director said at an In Conversation event at the the Singapore International Film Festival on Saturday. “The ideal is that after viewers finish watching, they remember that child’s smile and cry.”

Related Stories

Record and Song of the Year Grammy Predictions: With Ella Langley, Taylor Swift, the Two Olivias and Other Frontrunners in the Race, Expect a Nail-Biter

The festival presented Kore-eda with its Cinema Honorary Award at the National Museum of Singapore before an onstage conversation with festival chair Boo Junfeng, the filmmaker behind “Apprentice.” Introduced in 2014, the award is the festival’s top honor and recognizes lasting contributions to Asian cinema. Previous recipients include Im Kwon-taek, Garin Nugroho, Jafar Panahi and Deepa Mehta.

Popular on Variety

Kore-eda said his methods with children have grown more flexible. Through “Shoplifters” and the films he made abroad, “The Truth” and “Broker,” he did not hand children scripts. Instead, he rewrote dialogue around the personality and vocabulary of the children he met at auditions, so that they only spoke lines they could say with conviction, and then fed them lines on set or described a situation and let them talk freely.

On “Monster,” he gave the young cast scripts, judging that the subject was risky enough that separating the children from their roles was safer. He now decides child by child and film by film, he said.

Two directors shaped that approach. Hou Hsiao-hsien , Kore-eda said, joins in when children are playing in a scene, slips out once the camera is rolling and lets them keep going – a trick Kore-eda now uses himself.

From Ken Loach , he took a lesson about judgment. In Loach’s “Kes,” a boy discovers the bird he has raised dumped in a trash can after his brother kills it, and the young actor’s reaction looks nothing like a performance. When Kore-eda met Loach about 20 years ago, while he was making “Nobody Knows” and wrestling with similar questions, Loach told him he had only instructed the boy to go and look for the missing bird. Asked how he had weighed the ethics of that, Loach said he understood the risk but was confident that his relationship with the boy could repair any hurt. Kore-eda said the lesson was that Loach was weighing each shot as he went.

“I keep it firmly in mind that judging things that way – it worked on the last shoot so it will work this time, or a method that worked with the last child will work with this one – is the most dangerous thing in directing children,” he said.

He never gets angry with children or rushes them, he said, and he doesn’t lie to them. “The ideal is that a child ends the day saying, ‘Today’s shoot was fun, I’m looking forward to tomorrow,’” he said.

Some children simply won’t listen, he added, in which case he turns that into the role. During auditions for “Like Father, Like Son,” one boy answered every question, including his name and where he was from, with “Why?” Staff thought communication was impossible, but Kore-eda was drawn to him and wrote a character who answers everything with “Why?”

Kore-eda called himself a fan of Hou rather than someone he was influenced by, but the Taiwanese director also changed how he approaches a scene. Hou read the script for Kore-eda’s 1995 debut “Maborosi,” which won the Golden Osella in Venice, and introduced him to a composer, so Kore-eda showed him the finished film. Hou critiqued it severely, he said. “I was deflated. But what he told me was absolutely right.”

Kore-eda said he had drawn up a meticulous blueprint and that his crew did professional work to realize it, but he failed to update the plan on set. Hou asked whether he had storyboarded every scene and shot it exactly as drawn. He had.

“Where you shoot a scene from – you go into the location, feel the space, see the light falling there, and that’s when you first decide how the actors move,” Kore-eda recalled Hou telling him. “Once the actors’ movements are decided, only then do you decide the camera position. You have to do it in that order. You know that, you made documentaries.”

“Now I’m truly grateful he said that to me, but at the time it really got to me,” Kore-eda said. “I swore I’d never draw storyboards again.”

Kore-eda said he sees his two 2026 films, “Sheep in the Box” and “Look Back,” as a return to his roots. “Sheep in the Box,” which competed in Cannes, follows a couple whose 7-year-old son died two years earlier and who take in a humanoid robot built from his data. Despite the AI element, Kore-eda said, the film is about grief work.

“It’s a story about how to properly say goodbye to the dead, so I feel it actually ended up closest to what I tried to do in my debut,” he said.

“Look Back,” his live-action adaptation of Fujimoto Tatsuki’s manga about two girls bound by a love of drawing manga, played in competition at Venice and opens in Singapore on Oct. 29 after playing at the festival. On it, he said, he went back to the documentary thinking of his early films, treating the camera as an eye and simply asking where to watch the subject from.

“So I think the second half of my career probably starts next year,” he said.

Kore-eda said he writes best on long flights and in spare hours at hotels abroad, and has been writing on his current trip from London to Thailand and Singapore. He hopes to be shooting one project around this time next year at the earliest, or the year after if that proves difficult.

Thirty years after he started making films, the growing number of career awards leaves him uneasy, he said. “I feel like I still have about half my career left, and yet it kind of feels like I’m being told it’s time to graduate,” he said.

Kore-eda said he has little interest in AI, even though “Sheep in the Box” features a child brought back through generative AI. At a producer’s suggestion, he let an AI read his script for the first time. “At first it told me, ‘This is wonderful, it’s a sure thing for the Cannes Film Festival,’” he said. He ended the exercise after concluding the AI had probably never had a film experience big enough to change its life.

Kore-eda said he never tries to work out what audiences want, citing advice from a senior colleague he admired in his television days, when ratings were treated as everything. “He told me, ‘If you think of them as viewers, it won’t reach anyone,’” Kore-eda said. “He said to picture one person’s face and make it for them.”

Asked what dish he would choose for the afterlife, a nod to his 1998 film “After Life,” Kore-eda said he probably wouldn’t eat anything once he was dead. His last meal before dying, though, is already decided: the tenzaru soba at Sunaba, a noodle restaurant in Tokyo’s Akasaka district, where a senior producer took him when he was a young assistant director who had gone days without going home.

“The soba I ate there was the best I’ve had in my life, and it still is,” he said. “I want to eat that one more time at the end.”

article_text:
Prominent Polish documentarist Michał Marczak – a Sundance Film Festival prizewinner with “ All These Sleepless Nights ” – is set to make his narrative feature debut with “Perfection,” a buzzy drama about hipster millennials in Berlin, based on Italian author Vincenzo Latronico’s eponymous novel that was shortlisted for the 2025 International Booker Prize.

German producer Roman Paul, of Razor Film (“Quo Vadis, Aida?”), Britain’s Andrea Calderwood, head of prominent London-based indie Potboiler Productions, and Italy’s Marta Donzelli, partner in Vivo Film (“The Last One for the Road”), have teamed up on the high-profile project. Donzelli was instrumental in winning the bidding war for the book’s rights that were negotiated by Claire Sabatié-Garat of the Italian Literary Agency on behalf of Latronico and the producers.

Related Stories

Netflix Stock Deflates to Two-Year Low. What Will It Take to Revive Revenue Growth?

Netflix Grapples With Digital-Ad Squeeze Amid Widening Glut of Streaming Commercials

“Perfection” – which has been translated and sold in more than 40 countries – turns on a millennial expat couple named Anna and Tom who are living their dream during the 2010s in Berlin. “Their life as young digital creatives revolves around slow cooking, Danish furniture, sexual experimentation and the city’s 24-hour party scene – an ideal existence shared by an entire generation and tantalizingly lived out on social media,” says the synopsis of the book’s English-language edition.

“But beyond the images, dissatisfaction and ennui burgeon. Work becomes repetitive. Friends move back home, have children, grow up. Frustrated that their progressive politics amount to little more in practice than boycotting Uber, tipping in cash, or never eating tuna, Anna and Tom make a fruitless attempt at political activism,” it goes on to add. “Feeling increasingly trapped in their picture-perfect life, the couple takes ever more radical steps in the pursuit of an authenticity and a sense of purpose perennially beyond their grasp.”

“I’ve been living in Berlin since 1998 and with all the younger producers in my company – who are either expats or born there – we had long been looking for an original IP about what went on there in the 2010s when Berlin really meant something to the world,” Paul told Variety, speaking on the sidelines of the Rome MIA Market .

“In those early days of social media people were more idealistic about what it could achieve and how it allowed them to live the digital nomad life,” Calderwood said. “Because it is such a perfectly formed novel, we feel there is a way to make a perfectly formed film, which will have universal access and appeal,” she added.

Marczak, who won 2016 directing prize in the Sundance World Cinema – documentary category for “All These Sleepless Nights,” is known for his hybrid style that blurs the lines between documentary and fiction. His most recent work is multiple prize-winning “ Closure ,” about a teenager who disappears and his father’s relentless search for him, which also bowed at Sundance and will be released in U.S. theaters via 1-2 Special on Oct. 28.

Marczak’s films are “hybrid films, some of which focus on young people, for whom he has a very good eye and ear,” Paul noted, adding that “his sense of visuals is sublime.” He also pointed out that Marczak lived in Berlin and shot a film there, 2012 doc “Fuck for Forest” about a real-life Berlin-based non-governmental organization that raises money for environmental causes by producing and selling eco-pornography online.

Marczak and a still-to-be-determined screenwriter will write the English-language screenplay for “Perfection” that, unlike Latronico’s atmospheric novel, will include dialogues.

The producers are “in constant dialogue” with Latronico who “has been very supportive of our choice of director,” though the book’s author will not be directly involved in the screenplay, they said.

The “Perfection” project is in early development with Marczak attached as director, the next step being the writing of a treatment, followed by a screenplay.

“We are taking a step-by-step approach, building the development package before we take it to the market,” said Calderwood, who noted that “there is plenty of interest in the IP.”

article_text:
Der Hype um den Teppich von Bayeux im British Museum in London übertrifft alle Erwartungen. Aber warum stehen die Briten stundenlang für ein Stück Stoff aus dem elften Jahrhundert an? Vielleicht, weil das Werk von gestern und heute zugleich erzählt

"Es tut uns wirklich leid für alle, die keine guten Erfahrungen gemacht haben", erklärte Nicholas Cullinan gegenüber der BBC: "Unser Fokus liegt ganz darauf, daraus zu lernen und es besser zu machen." Angesprochen wurde der Direktor des British Museum auf die frustrierten Kunstinteressierten, die stundenlang in der Warteschlange vor dem Prachtbau ausgeharrt hatten. Am Ende wurden viele von ihnen weggeschickt, weil die Öffnungszeiten des Museums für ein "privates Ereignis" abgekürzt worden waren. Nun sollen die Abgewiesenen bei der Vergabe neuer Zeitfenster bevorzugt werden.

Dass ein Museum vom Publikum geradezu überrannt wird, ist alles andere als der Normalzustand in den Kunsttempeln dieser Welt. Doch genau das passiert in diesem Herbst, seit die Ausstellung des sogenannten Teppichs von Bayeux im British Museum vor rund vier Wochen begonnen hat.

Mit erheblichem Interesse der Öffentlichkeit war gerechnet worden, seit sich die Verhandlungen über die Ausleihe des bestickten Stoffstreifens – denn nüchtern betrachtet handelt es sich genau darum – aus seiner französischen Heimat Bayeux nach England konkretisiert hatten. Der tatsächliche Hype aber übertrifft alle Erwartungen.

Das Trauma der Briten

Die umfangreiche, an brutalen Details nicht gerade arme Schilderung der Eroberung des altenglischen Königreichs durch bestens bewaffnete Angreifer aus der Normandie im Jahr 1066 zielt genau auf das Trauma aller Bewohner der britischen Inseln in den 960 Jahren seither: von Invasoren von "jenseits des Meeres" überfallen und beherrscht zu werden. Denn der Ausgangspunkt dieser kollektiven Furcht ist genau das: der siegreiche Überfall durch die Truppen eines normannischen Herzogs, der seither nur als William the Conqueror, Wilhelm der Eroberer, bekannt ist.

Wie dieses Ur-Ereignis der neuenglischen und bis heute bruchlos andauernden Geschichte ablief, haben fleißige Frauenhände auf 70 Meter Leinentuch gestickt: im wahrsten Sinne des Wortes ein strip , aber kein komischer, sondern ein bluttriefend ernster. Wo andere historische Ereignisse allein in fragwürdigen Erzählungen überliefert sind, liegt hier ein regelrechter Augenzeugenbericht vor. Denn der nach seinem normannischen Aufbewahrungsort Bayeux benannte Stoffstreifen ist unmittelbar nach dem Ereignis angefertigt worden, kaum dass die Truppen des "Eroberers" sich in England festgesetzt hatten.

So weit, so historisch. Was aber treibt heutige Schaulustige ins Museum, lässt sie stundenlang in Schlangen ausharren oder im Internet wahre Fantasiesummen für die Übernahme eines gebuchten Slots bieten?

Nichts ist so erfolgreich wie der Erfolg

Zum einen – und das ist die oberflächlichste Erklärung – gilt der alte Spruch, dass nichts so erfolgreich ist wie der Erfolg. An ihm wollen alle teilhaben, und wo alle hingehen, will man nicht abseitsstehen. Diesen Effekt hat als erster Thomas Hoving, der legendäre Direktor des Metropolitan Museum in New York genutzt, als er in den 1970er-Jahren die Wanderausstellung der Goldfunde aus dem Grab des Pharaos Tutanchamun wie ein neues Auto oder Waschmittel bewarb und "King Tut!" zum Ereignis der Saison hochjazzte.

Sensationen nutzen sich ab, der Teppich von Bayeux aber behält seine Anziehungskraft; so wie auch die Goldmasken des altägyptischen Pharaos ein dauerhaftes Faszinosum bleiben. Das verweist auf eine Eigenschaft, die solchen Objekten nicht einmal unmittelbar anzusehen sein muss, die aber gewusst und erspürt wird: ihre Originalität.

Es handelt sich um historische, einmalige Objekte, die nie vollständig nachgemacht werden können, eben weil sie eine gewisse Aura umgibt. Den Stoffstreifen von Bayeux gibt es kein zweites Mal, er ist singulär, er ist ein unnachahmliches und eben auch unwiederbringliches Einzelstück.

Der Stoff ist selbst Geschichte

Und er besitzt, was nicht ganz dasselbe ist, Authentizität. Das ist eine Eigenschaft, die an Bedeutung zunehmend gewinnt, ja mehr unsere mediale Gegenwart von fake news und computergenerierten Surrogaten bevölkert wird. Der normannische Stoff entstammt der Zeit, von der er spricht. Das Objekt und seine Aussage sind in ihrer zeitlichen Dimension kongruent. In ihm, dem Stoff von Bayeux, tritt dem Betrachter die erzählte Geschichte in gegenständlicher Form unmittelbar entgegen. Das Textil ist selbst Geschichte.

Doch seine Anziehungskraft reicht noch tiefer. Es gibt ein breites, wiewohl oft verschüttetes Interesse an der Historie, und vor allem an derjenigen, die mit einem selbst zu tun hat. Woher kommen wir? Diese Frage ist so alt wie das Bewusstsein von Geschichtlichkeit selbst. Es bedeutet, dass es ein Vorher und ein Nachher gibt, eine Entwicklung von A nach B, mag sie gut oder schlecht, strahlend oder katastrophal gewesen sein. Es ist das Bewusstsein einer zwar nicht gleichförmigen, wohl aber linear ablaufenden Zeit, in der Ereignisse Folgen haben und in vielen Fällen bis in die Gegenwart nachwirken.

Ohne die normannischen Eroberer gäbe es die ganze 1000-jährige Geschichte Englands seither nicht, was im Umkehrschluss bedeutet, dass das Heute unmittelbar auf das Damals zurückzuführen ist. Das ist es, was Menschen spüren, wenn sie den Teppich von Bayeux betrachten: dass sie selbst mit dem Ereignis in Verbindung stehen, das da in gestickter Form überliefert wird.

Man kann sich selbst beim Verstehen der Geschichte zusehen

Darüber hinaus – und das betrifft die Anziehung auf ein jüngeres Publikum – ist die Form der Überlieferung im Falle Bayeux so eingängig wie selten. Die fortlaufend erzählte, von links nach rechts voranschreitende Erzählung kommt den Sehgewohnheiten jüngerer Betrachter geradezu ideal entgegen. Es gibt viel zu entdecken, und das Gezeigte ist unmittelbar verständlich. 627 Personen, 190 Pferde, 41 Schiffe wurden auf dem Textil gezählt. Randereignisse bereichern und vertiefen die Haupthandlung, Emotionen und Empathie werden geweckt, wie beim Detail des in Brand gesteckten Hauses mit seinen todgeweihten Bewohnern.

Im Nacheinander der einzelnen Bilder konstituiert sich im Betrachter die Gesamtheit des historischen Vorgangs, der da erzählt wird. Man kann sich gewissermaßen selbst beim Verstehen zusehen.

Geschichte als solche war nicht immer gleichermaßen bedeutsam. Erst das 19. Jahrhundert war geradezu obsessiv im Umgang mit ihr. Nationalgeschichte ist zumeist ein Produkt dieser Zeit, sie hat Eingang in Schulbücher gefunden und ist ins kollektive Bewusstsein eingesunken. Der Teppich von Bayeux erzählt eine Begebenheit, die zur britischen Identitätserzählung wurde. In den Besuchermassen, die vor dem British Museum ausharren und sich schließlich an der schier endlosen Vitrine entlang schieben, tritt dieses kollektive Bewusstsein als zugleich individuell wie gemeinschaftlich Erlebtes zutage. Der Stoff von Bayeux erzählt von damals. Aber er erzählt zugleich von heute.

article_text:
Picture a large pavilion, strings of bare bulbs hanging from the ceiling, and long tables covered in white cloth. On them, prints are laid out edge to edge, wooden boxes stand open, and books are propped up like small altars. Behind each table, a photographer waits. In front, visitors lean in, turn a page, ask a question. A reviewer from a major publication stops, then stays. This is the Portfolio Walk, the public face of Review Santa Fe. Each year, the evening draws crowds. CENTER says more than 1,000 people can pass through in a single night.

A professional crossroads

Review Santa Fe is first of all a working conference. One hundred photographers, selected by an independent committee, travel to New Mexico with a project they hope will find a wider audience. There, they sit down with the people who can help it do so.

This year, CENTER welcomes 19 editors, including representatives of National Geographic , The New York Times , Oxford American and NPR. They are joined by 10 museum curators, 7 book publishers and 9 gallery representatives. That makes 45 reviewers, who spend the weekend looking at work and deciding which of it deserves to travel further. The result is nearly 1,000 one-on-one meetings in four days.

Participation is by application. A selection committee of three industry professionals ranks the submitted projects, and invited photographers then pay a fee for their package of reviews. CENTER says scholarships and payment plans are available.

The format reflects CENTER’s own history. Founded in 1994, the Santa Fe non-profit supports socially and environmentally engaged lens-based projects through education, funding and partnerships. Review Santa Fe is its largest event of the year.

Six award and grant recipients

The weekend opens on October 23 at CENTER Gallery with The Conditions of Seeing , an exhibition of the 2026 award and grant recipients: Marcus DeSieno, Anna Mia Davidson, Leonard Suryajaya, Peter Teh, Ville Varumo and Volodymyr Voznyy.

The show gathers landscape, portraiture, staged scenes, diary-like image-making and socially engaged practice. What links them is a question: under what conditions do people, places and selves become visible? Their work looks at how seeing is shaped by political systems, inherited histories, environmental change, cultural assumptions, relationships, memory and care.

On the morning of October 25, Marcus DeSieno, a Project Launch Grant recipient, presents Geography of Disappearance: Migrant Deaths on the US/Mexico Border . The United Nations has described the border as the deadliest land crossing in the world. DeSieno photographs along it, going to the exact places where the bodies of unknown migrants were found. He locates them using autopsy reports and data collected by humanitarian organisations and by local and state police. The photographs, he writes in his project statement, serve “as a space for somber remembrance of the deceased.”

Open to all

Most of the public programme is free. The Portfolio Walk takes place on October 24 and lets visitors speak directly with the hundred photographers. The work covers a wide range of contemporary photography on social, environmental and political subjects. It can be previewed beforehand on the Review Santa Fe Listing website. On October 26, a panel with the reviewers, moderated by Thomas Werner, closes the weekend with a discussion of how photographic projects get published and exhibited.

Online and in-person events are both offered this year.

The Review Santa Fe Photo Symposium takes place from October 23 to 26, 2026, in Santa Fe, New Mexico (USA). The full programme is on CENTER’s website , and the work of the hundred photographers can be previewed on the Review Santa Fe Listing . Applications for the 2026 edition closed on February 28, and the next call for entry opens in January 2027 on CENTER’s application page .

article_text:
More than a year after his death, Ozzy Osbourne ‘s fans can relive his final performance through an upcoming concert film .

Sharon Osbourne recently shared her reaction to Ozzy & Black Sabbath : Back to the Beginning , premiering Oct. 25 in theaters, adding that her late husband would feel like “one lucky son of a bitch” after seeing the documentary from director Ben Wainwright-Pearce ( Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour , George Michael: The Faith Tour ).

“It was very hard to watch a lot of this film. I had to, but it was very, very hard,” Osbourne told Rolling Stone . “It’s bittersweet. It’s amazing. Everything about the show was amazing and just a joyous occasion and one that will go down in music history. I’m proud of that and that it was for my husband, and I’m so thankful to everyone that took part in it, for their time, their effort, their giving.”

Related Stories

Ozzy Osbourne Dies: Black Sabbath Frontman, Solo Singer & Reality TV Star Was 76

Jack Osbourne Says Ozzy Movie Won’t Be “Artsy, Esoteric Biopic”: “Not What The Fans Want”

Noting that Ozzy “was in hospital for a week in England” before the July 5, 2025 concert, Sharon recalled his doctors “advised us not to do the show,” but he was determined.

Watch on Deadline

“They said it would kill him. We were all together and Ozzy said, ‘It’s not an option. It’s what I want,'” she revealed. “He said, ‘I know I’m dying. If I miss a few months of my life, I want to go this way. This is what I want.’ It was his wishes and we went through it. He said to me, ‘Another six months, what’s it going to do for me?'”

Ozzy died at age 76 weeks later on July 22, 2025, suffering a heart attack after living with coronary artery’s disease and Parkinson’s disease.

When asked what Ozzy would think of the concert film, Sharon surmised, “He would say, ‘How lucky am I?’ He goes, ‘I’m one lucky son of a bitch.’ And he knew it. He never took anything for granted, ever.”

The late Black Sabbath frontman’s family is also developing a biopic about him, five years after Sony Pictures and Polygram Entertainment were said to be in the works on a project.

article_text:
日本ならではの、ユニークな「現代ジュエリー」の生い立ちと表現を見る

京都国立近代美術館 で 「ジュエリーは、誰を夢みる」 が、開催されている。日本では愛子さま（天皇皇后両陛下長女）がティアラを新調されない質素さが好感をもって受け止められるように、欧米でのような権威やアイデンティティの象徴たるジュエリー文化はない。

とはいえ、ジュエリー文化が「ない」のではない。日本でジュエリーは、欧米とはまったく異なるユニークな歴史を歩んできた。そもそも日本のジュエリー文化には、1000年以上のブランクがある。古墳時代の豪族たちは金製品やガラス玉、水晶などで身を飾り、また埋葬の際には副葬品として埋めていたが、これ以降、装いは着物が中心になり、埋葬も火葬が主流になったため、装身具も副葬品もなくなった。江戸時代には水晶や珊瑚、真珠で、簪、帯留や印籠などの装飾品もつくられたが、それを幕府の奢侈禁止令（しゃしきんしれい）が抑圧した。明治時代に西洋のジュエリーが流入するが、まだ女性たちは和装が主流だったため、身につけられるのは結婚指輪どまり。しかしそれもまた、二度の大戦のあいだに「贅沢は敵だ」と言われてしまう。ジュエリーは、長い受難の時期を過ごしてきた。

日本では、1964年の日本ジュエリーデザイナー協会（JJDA）の設立が、ジュエリーを素材の価値だけでなく造形・表現の分野としてとらえる動きを広める契機となった。同時代の美術とも呼応する日本の「コンテンポラリージュエリー」は、戦後に社会やアートシーン、価値観が目まぐるしく変化するなかで育ってきた。本展ではその成り立ちと国際的な交流、日本人作家の活躍までを350件もの作品から紹介する。

技術とデザインを重視した日本の現代ジュエリー。志は「日本を豊かに美しくしたい」

展示の第1章では、日本のコンテンポラリージュエリーを牽引した、東京藝術大学名誉教授の平松保城（1926〜2012）と、山梨県立宝石美術専門学校の設立に尽力した菱田安彦（1927〜81）の作品が紹介される。平松は、まだ敗戦ムードが残る50年代、「人間にとって、社会に対して価値のあるものを作りたい」と、金属でシンプルな装身具を作り始めた。日本での作家性を持ったジュエリーの始まりには、豊かさと美しさを求める気持ちがあった。作品を見ると、平松、菱田ともに、彫金や鍛金の高度な技術を駆使している。商業的な宝飾品も注目されつつあるなか、日本のコンテンポラリージュエリーは宝石ではなく、金工の技と研ぎ澄まされたデザインが主役だった。

金工の技術を母として生まれた日本のコンテンポラリージュエリーは、「工芸／ジュエリー」というふたつのジャンルが絡み合い、また別々のものとも見なされながら展開されてゆく。そうした揺らぎの中にあることは、見る側には自由度を高め、作り手には問題意識となっただろう。その問いを反芻しつつ、先駆者たちの技巧的な作品を鑑賞したい。

コンセプチュアルアートと連動する、「きれいなだけじゃない」ジュエリー

社会が豊かになるにつれて、オリジナリティのある現代的な感覚のジュエリーは、ちょっとした流行のファッションアイテムとして受け入れられ、1970年から1986年には西武百貨店渋谷店で「国際ジュウリー・アート展」が好評のうちに開催された。

ジュエリーの普及とともに、70年代後半から「コンセプトをもったジュエリー」も登場する。作家たちのなかには、「ジュエリーにまつわる意味や価値を、ジュエリーを通して問う」ような批評的な作品に取り組み始める者もいた。「ジュエリーとは何か？」を根底から疑うような、身につけられないもの、姿のないものもあった。ピエール・ドゥガンの《木箱型の手袋》《木製のカヌー型手袋》は、素材も姿もジュエリー離れした作品で、タイトルは謎かけのようだ。伊藤一廣は、海岸に白い木綿の布を置いた《シージュエリー》など、インスタレーション的な大型作品を発表した。

コンセプチュアルジュエリー作家、オットー・キュンツリの、モノを言う作品

こうした「コンセプチュアルジュエリー」の流れを牽引した作家に、スイス出身のオットー・キュンツリ（1948〜）がいる。ミュンヘン造形芸術大学でジュエリークラスの教授を長年務め、日本の専門学校「ヒコ・みずのジュエリーカレッジ」とともに、東京、ミュンヘン、アムステルダムの3校合同展を開催するなどして交流し、日本でも多くの作家をインスパイアした。

キュンツリ自身の作品も、ジュエリーの象徴性や価値を皮肉るウィットに富んだものだ。ジュエリーを誇示する虚栄心を、金塊のかたちのチョコレートの空箱であらわした《スイス・ゴールド》。展覧会ヴィジュアルにも使用されている《ハート》は、幸福の象徴を身につけられることを拒否するかのように、10cm近い大きさのブローチにした。

《チェーン》は、使用しなくなった結婚指輪を募集し48個つなげた作品。傍らには、指輪が要らなくなった理由を記したノートが添えられる。死別あり離婚あり。「永遠の誓い」の輝きがほろ苦い。

キュンツリの作品を筆頭に、展示にはコンセプチュアルな作品が数多く並んでいて、「ジュエリーのコンセプトを読む」という刺激的な体験が続く。現代アート界での傾向に連動したものではあるが、Tokyo Art Beatの読者なら、こうした「ジュエリーしばり」のコンセプチュアルアートは、新鮮に感じられるのではないだろうか。

日本にも、技もコンセプトも冴えるジュエリー作家が育っている。そのひとりが田口史樹だ。《Tiara?!》は、野球のキャップのかたちをしたシルバーのヘッドピース。焼き付けた銀の粉を藍に染めるという技術を駆使し、大衆的なブランドアイテムとロイヤルの象徴とを対峙させる。

記憶のアートとしてのジュエリー、身体表現とジュエリー

ジュエリーは「形見」として受け継がれることも多く、「永遠」の象徴でもある。そこに、パーソナルな「記憶」を重ねる作品が、テッド・ノーテン《Chisaka's Bag（千栄のバッグ）》、ベルンハルト・ショービンガー《消しゴムのネックレス》。誰かの身近にあったオブジェが永遠の命を持つジュエリーにトランスフォームする。

ジュエリーは、アートだけでなく同時代のファションやパフォーミングアーツからも刺激を受けた。80年代は身体への意識が高まり、バレエ、音楽、ファッションと領域をまたいだコラボレーション表現が盛んに上演された時代でもある。ジュエリー表現でも、身体を拡張するような、ボディ・コンシャスな作品が作られた。

身体に装着する矯正ギアのような作品で、ジュエリーによる自己変容を試みるのが新里明子だ。容姿と自信の関係を研究するなかで、不安定なアイデンティティを支え、自信を与えてくれるギアとしてのジュエリーを制作した。顔を改変するジュエリー、笑みが描かれたマスク、身につけると矯正具のように元気な表情とポーズになる《自信増幅器》。問答無用に自己肯定感を上げるジュエリーだ。

異素材＆リサイクル素材で、ジュエリーを開放する

アーティストたちのジュエリーへの冒険をたっぷり見た展示の終盤、ジュエリーの解放ともいえる作品が展示されていた。2台のテーブルに広げられている嶺脇美貴子の作品は、プラモデルや台所用具をカットして作ったリングやネックレスだ。

ものを用途から解放し、また、ジュエリーを高価さや非日常のイメージから解放する。この自由さは、日本のコンテンポラリージュエリーがその黎明期から掲げていた、「宝石よりも技術とデザインを重視すること」「社会の豊かさのために」という志をしっかりと受け止めているように思える。

一般的には宝飾品に使われない素材から作られたジュエリーは、一度廃棄された後も生活感や感情を手繰り寄せる装置に生まれ変わる。

現代ジュエリー専門ギャラリーで、個別の作家を深める

多彩な現代ジュエリー作品の作家や、マーケットについてもっと知りたい、コレクションしたいという人には京都のC.A.J.（コンテンポラリーアートジュエリー）を訪ねて欲しい。オープンして20年。「ジュエリーは、誰を夢みる」展にも出品されている第一線の日本人作家たちの作品も取り扱う。（11月8日まで三島一能展を開催）

「ヨーロッパの専門家からは、『日本のジュエリーはコンセプトが弱い』と言われますが、私自身は、テクニカルなものを見せていくこと、美しいものを伝えることも大切だと思っています」と、オーナーのコンドウヒトミさん。ジュエリーは技術と美しさ、さらにコンセプトが揃わなければ成立しない。しかし鑑賞のハードルも高いと思ってしまうのは残念だ。「ジュエリーって、“女の人が身につけるもの”で、終わっちゃう。現代美術の人に話すと、”工芸でしょ”で終わっちゃう。日本では陶芸のオブジェが認められているように、海外ではジュエリーで同じようなことが成立しているんです」。ジュエリーは、身につけて楽しく、工芸としてもアートとしても鑑賞できる。

article_text:
Surveying the incredible six-decade career of contemporary artist Nalini Malani, this exhibition is characterised by its ability to evoke both beauty and discomfort.

As a global storyteller based in Mumbai, Malani’s work is deeply influenced by her own lived experience as a child refugee of India’s Partition. Her practice centres on rewriting Western and Eastern history, myths and literature in a way that prompts viewers to question the world around them. With this exhibition, Malani addresses the complexity of our times and reveals the hopeful conviction that guides her practice: ‘The future is female, there is no other way’.

Known in India since the late sixties for her pioneering multidisciplinary approach, Malani gained international recognition with signature monumental multi-media works and installations such as Mother India: Transactions in the Construction of Pain , and In Search of Vanished Blood. These works will be presented in the show alongside her recent iPad animation series Can You Hear Me?

Designed specially with the artist, this is Malani’s largest survey exhibition to date, compromising almost 200 works. These include rarely seen watercolour diaries, black and white films, camera-less photography, large-scale video-based works, innovative reverse paintings and a newly-commissioned wall drawing and performance piece.
